canonical_goal: Close the post-WAVE-108 ExAIS remaining roadmap to production-readiness governance by reconciling stale tracker claims, finishing repo-buildable release/ops/model/admin gaps, and separating external deployment proof gates without reopening the completed OpenAI parity train.

tickets.title: Reconcile reindex repair status
tickets.goal: Resolve the stale tracker disagreement where the current trail/README describe reindex repair as implemented while the completion matrix still lists the reindex repair worker as incomplete.
tickets.acceptance: A focused proof demonstrates that non-indexed dense and sparse chunks are discovered, repaired or replayed through the worker/maintenance path, marked indexed, and cleaned up from stale backend state; the roadmap docs agree on the resulting status and cite the proof command.

tickets.title: Reconcile OpenAPI contract status
tickets.goal: Resolve the stale tracker disagreement where OpenAI-compatible parity work is broadly recorded as implemented while the matrix still calls out the full OpenAPI contract as incomplete.
tickets.acceptance: Generated OpenAPI output covers every documented native and OpenAI-compatible route with stable request/response components, a regression check fails on contract drift, and the roadmap docs agree on whether any explicit contract gaps remain.

tickets.title: Enforce Alembic migration discipline
tickets.goal: Replace ad hoc raw SQL migration loops with an Alembic-governed migration path suitable for production snapshots, rollback planning, and CI enforcement.
tickets.acceptance: Alembic is the authoritative migration entrypoint, production-like upgrade checks run in CI, rollback or forward-fix rules are documented, and migration drift/raw-loop bypasses are caught by a repeatable check.

tickets.title: Automate image provenance release
tickets.goal: Finish the versioned image release lane with CI image builds, digest publication, digest pinning, and signed release verification for micro-production cells.
tickets.acceptance: CI builds the versioned API, worker, model-gateway, admin-ui, and instance-agent images, emits a digest manifest, signs or records verifiable provenance for each image, and cell startup/upgrade rejects unpinned or unverifiable images.

tickets.title: Implement encrypted secrets workflow
tickets.goal: Turn the production secrets lane from env-file placeholders into an encrypted, auditable workflow for customer cells.
tickets.acceptance: A production cell can be configured from encrypted SOPS/age or Vault-backed secrets, preflight validates secret references without printing secret values, plaintext production secrets are rejected, and rotation/runbook steps are documented.

tickets.title: Wire backup integrations
tickets.goal: Implement the actual backup integrations behind the existing backup/restore runbooks for metadata, vectors, sparse indexes, object storage, configs, and audit artifacts.
tickets.acceptance: Backup commands write verifiable artifacts to a configured object/offsite target for Postgres, Qdrant, OpenSearch, MinIO/object storage, config/secrets metadata, and audit exports; restore preflight can enumerate and validate those artifacts without restoring them.

tickets.title: Ship observability dashboards
tickets.goal: Promote the minimal metrics hook into production observability dashboards and alert rules for API, ingestion, retrieval, indexes, storage, security, cost, and backup freshness.
tickets.acceptance: Prometheus-compatible metrics are scraped by a local cell observability stack, dashboards expose the production-ready delta's required panels, alert rules cover the documented failure modes, and a smoke test proves at least one API, worker, index, and backup metric is visible.

tickets.title: Harden admin sessions
tickets.goal: Replace dev-header admin UI identity with production auth/session or API-key principal resolution while keeping the backend as the security authority.
tickets.acceptance: The admin UI no longer depends on dev tenant/business/user headers in production mode, session/OIDC/API-key principal context is resolved by the API, unauthorized admin flows fail closed, and UI/API tests cover login/session expiry and principal-scoped requests.

tickets.title: Expose fleet version UI
tickets.goal: Complete the admin production contract for instance switching and fleet/version visibility across micro-production cells.
tickets.acceptance: An authorized admin can select an instance/business vault, view running component versions and image digests, see upgrade/deployment records, and identify cells that are behind or unverifiable without relying on shell access.

tickets.title: Implement live bakeoff fan-out
tickets.goal: Finish the eval lane that must run live retrieval/provider fan-out before any fine-tuning work is promoted.
tickets.acceptance: A bakeoff run can fan out the same golden query set across multiple retrieval/model candidates, persist comparable quality/latency/cost metrics, select or reject a winner by policy, and prove with deterministic test providers plus a documented live-provider command.

tickets.title: Implement private endpoint adapters
tickets.goal: Finish private model endpoint adapters for RunPod, TEI, Infinity, and compatible self-hosted embedding/rerank backends behind the model gateway.
tickets.acceptance: Registered private endpoints expose health, p95 latency, max security level, region, model revision, and auth secret references; embedding/rerank calls normalize through the gateway contract; failed health disables routing or triggers policy fallback.

tickets.title: Prove external registry push
tickets.goal: Capture the operator-dependent proof that versioned images can be pushed to Docker Hub or a private external registry after credentials are available.
tickets.acceptance: With operator-supplied registry credentials, the documented push command publishes the versioned image set, records immutable digests, proves pull-by-digest from a clean environment, and stores the proof output without claiming VPS readiness.

tickets.title: Prove customer cell launch
tickets.goal: Capture the operator-dependent proof that a chosen VPS or customer micro-production cell can run the externally published images.
tickets.acceptance: On the target VPS/customer host, the runbook pulls pinned images, boots the compose cell with production preflight passing, proves API/admin/worker/model-gateway readiness, runs smoke retrieval, and records raw host/topology evidence.

tickets.title: Validate real providers
tickets.goal: Capture the operator-dependent proof that real provider credentials and endpoints work for OpenAI, RunPod, TEI, Infinity, and other approved providers.
tickets.acceptance: With live credentials/endpoints supplied, provider integration tests execute embedding and rerank calls through the gateway, enforce security-level routing policy, record latency/error/cost metadata, and identify any provider that remains unavailable or unapproved.

tickets.title: Prove external restore drill
tickets.goal: Capture the operator-dependent proof that backups can restore an external micro-production cell or staging clone, not only a local Docker environment.
tickets.acceptance: Using a real backup target and external cell topology, the runbook restores metadata, object artifacts, one Qdrant collection, one OpenSearch index, and config/secrets references, then runs retrieval/eval smoke checks against the restored environment.

tickets.title: Run corpus-scale load tests
tickets.goal: Capture the operator-dependent proof that the target corpus and workload meet the production latency, freshness, and indexing objectives.
tickets.acceptance: Against the selected corpus or a documented production-scale surrogate, ingestion and retrieval load tests report throughput, p95 search latency, p95 context-pack latency, queue freshness, index growth, provider latency, and failure modes against the documented SLO targets.

tickets.title: Prove DNS TLS secrets wiring
tickets.goal: Capture the operator-dependent proof that production DNS, TLS, and external secrets-manager wiring are correctly attached to the launched cell.
tickets.acceptance: For the chosen domain/cell, DNS resolves to the target host, HTTPS/TLS health checks pass without wildcard dev allowances, secrets-manager references resolve through preflight without value disclosure, and rollback/rotation steps are documented.
